content_blocks.title: Brain MRI Report – Impression & Findings
content_blocks.content:
Exam: MRI Brain W & W/O Contrast. Study Date: Dec 15, 2025. Contrast: 7 mL Gadobutrol (Single-Dose). Finalized: Dec 17, 2025. Indication: R79.89 (Other specified abnormal findings of blood chemistry); possible CSF leak. No prior comparison study available.

IMPRESSION:
1. No acute intracranial abnormality.
2. Mild nonspecific white matter signal changes, most likely sequela of microangiopathic ischemia.
3. Left cerebellar developmental venous anomaly (DVA).

KEY FINDINGS:
- Brain parenchyma: No mass, mass effect, midline shift, or intracranial hemorrhage. Normal posterior fossa. Unremarkable diffusion imaging.
- White matter: Mild ill-defined confluent T2/FLAIR signal hyperintensity in periventricular and subcortical white matter bilaterally; attributed to chronic microvascular ischemia.
- Venous anatomy: Left cerebellar DVA identified. No pachymeningeal enhancement (relevant to CSF leak workup).
- Auditory canals/petrous: No CPA/IAC mass. Bilateral thinning of the roof of the superior semicircular canal.
- Ventricles & sella: Normal for age. Normal pituitary.
- Vasculature & sinuses: Appropriate flow voids. Unremarkable paranasal sinuses.
- Calvarium & soft tissues: Normal.

Reading Physician: Sarah Meng, DO. Authorizing Provider: Jeffrey Liu, MD.

key_findings: This is a clinical diagnostic radiology report with no biotech, therapeutic, or drug development content.
No experimental data, model systems, efficacy measures, IP, regulatory submissions, or funding information are present.
The document is entirely a patient-level MRI interpretation and is not relevant to TRL assessment.

Key clinical findings include no acute intracranial abnormality, mild white matter changes consistent with microangiopathic ischemia, a left cerebellar DVA, and bilateral superior semicircular canal roof thinning — none of which pertain to a biotech project.
